management_steps.details: These indicate critical coronary occlusion without classic STE: (1) De Winter syndrome (V1-6 J-point depression with tall symmetric T waves), (2) Posterior STEMI (horizontal STD in V1-3, tall R in V1-2), (3) Wellens Sign A (biphasic T waves in V2-3) or Sign B (deeply inverted anterior T waves), (4) Shark fin pattern, (5) Hyperacute T waves.

Score >= 3 has 90% specificity for MI: (1) Criteria A (5 pts): concordant STE >= 1mm in any lead, (2) Criteria B (3 pts): concordant STD >= 1mm in V1, V2, or V3, (3) Criteria C (2 pts): discordant STE >= 5mm in any lead (Modified: STE >= 25% of preceding S-wave).

warnings: Failure to recognize STEMI equivalents leads to catastrophic treatment delays. Actively look for them in chest pain patients with normal or non-diagnostic ECGs.
